messages:
maria.c: Heads-up — since the canary we started getting a burst of 413s from /v1/embeddings. Looks like many clients are sending mixed-dim arrays (1536 + 768) and the splitter path isn't kicking in when the request exceeds our byte quota but lacks the shape header.

jamal: Yea saw the same in logs. The splitter currently only runs when `X-Vector-Shape` exists or when preflight returns required info. If clients omit shape we try best-effort and sometimes return 413.

oliver_k: Is the root problem missing client headers or the quota check order? We validate payload bytes before running splitter to avoid wasted CPU on huge blobs. Might need to swap or do a cheap shape probe first.

sophia: Quick telemetry: `embed.request.413` spiked by 8x in the last 30m and 64% of those have mixed dims in the payload sample. Suggest adding a metric broken down by `has_shape_header` vs `inferred_shape`.

jamal: Proposed fixes: 1) run a lightweight shape-detection pass (scan first 256KB) before the byte-quota check, 2) support an opt-in `?preflight=true` query so Console/SDKs can preview how we'd split, 3) emit `embed.splitter.preview_shown` event for UX metrics. Thoughts?

maria.c: I like 2+3 for UX. For the runtime change (1) we need to be careful about worst-case CPU cost. Maybe limit shape-detect to N vectors or bytes and fall back to quick rejection. Also we should avoid changing default latency for small requests.

oliver_k: For rollout: feature-flag the new preflight behaviour under `embed:preflight-shape-detect` and roll to canary for 10% tenants. Console will default to calling `?preflight=true` when user toggles "Auto-split preview" on a route.

sophia: UI idea: Console shows a split preview panel with a tiny histogram: "Estimated requests after split: 1 -> 3", estimated token cost delta, and a toggle to "apply auto-split on server". That lets ops decide before enabling. Also record preview accept/decline as a signal.

jamal: Here's the suggested preflight interface (server):

```http
POST /v1/embeddings?preflight=true
Content-Type: application/json
X-Api-Key: sk-***
{
  "input": [[...mixed arrays...]],
  "return_split_plan": true
}
```

response: `{ "split_plan": [{"requests":3, "per_request_bytes": 120000}], "est_cost": "0.012" }`

maria.c: That response shape is good. We also need a machine-readable rejection reason when we still return a 413: `{"error":"payload_too_large","reason":"no_shape_header_and_exceeds_quota"}` so SDKs can surface suggested remediation.

oliver_k: Telemetry keys to add: `embed.splitter.preview_shown`, `embed.splitter.preview_accepted`, `embed.request.rejection_reason:payload_too_large`, and tag `shape_source` = ["header","inferred","unknown"]. Will wire these into per-model dashboards.

sophia: UX question: when console shows "apply auto-split on server", should that set a per-route soft-quota (warn but allow) or an automatic rewrite? My vote: soft-rollout first (generate split plan at runtime), then allow hard-split if team opts in.

jamal: Agreed. Soft-rollout avoids surprising downstreams. Implementation notes for engineering: - preflight cheap-shape-detect should early-abort if input arrays > 2M elements or single blob > 10MB, - splitter must be idempotent, - log correlation id `x-rw-cid` in preview responses.

deploy-bot: feature flag `embed:preflight-shape-detect` created (ff-id: ff-9812), default off. Canary rollout window scheduled 2025-09-12 03:00 UTC.

maria.c: Action items: jamal -> prototype cheap-shape-detect + server preflight API, oliver_k -> Console preview mockups + API integration, sophia -> add telemetry events + dashboard tiles, maria.c -> PR for error shape and SDK guidance. I'll file issues and link here. :white_check_mark:
